==Problem 19==
Miguel is walking with his dog, Luna. When they reach the entrance to a park, Miguel throws a ball straight ahead and continues to walk at a steady pace. Luna sprints toward the ball, which stops by a tree. As soon as the dog reaches the ball, she brings it back to Miguel. Luna runs 5 times faster than Miguel walks. What fraction of the distance between the entrance and the tree does Miguel cover by the time Luna brings him the ball?

[[File:Amc 8 2026 q19.png | 650px]]

<imath>\textbf{(A) } \frac{1}{6}\qquad\textbf{(B) } \frac{1}{5}\qquad\textbf{(C) } \frac{1}{4}\qquad\textbf{(D) } \frac{1}{3}\qquad\textbf{(E) } \frac{2}{5}</imath>

==Solution==
Let Miguel's speed equal <imath>s</imath>. That makes Luna's speed <imath>5s</imath>. Let the distance between the park entrance and the tree be <imath>d</imath>. The total distance covered by Miguel and Luna is <imath>s + 5s = 6s</imath>, which is also equal to <imath>2d</imath>. Thus <imath>6s = 2d \Rightarrow s = \boxed{ \textbf{(D) } \frac{1}{3}}d</imath>.

~OlympiadMaster

==Solution 2==

The distance between the park entrance and the tree is <imath> x </imath>. Then, the rate that Miguel walks is <imath> v </imath>, and Luna runs at <imath> 5v </imath>. As Luna runs the distance <imath> x </imath> and back, she runs a total of <imath> 2x - m </imath> (where <imath> m </imath> is the amount that Miguel walks). Then, because <imath> d/s = t </imath> (where <imath> d </imath> is distance, <imath> t </imath> is time, and <imath> s </imath> is speed), It takes Luna <imath> \frac{2x - m}{5v} </imath> time to reach back to Miguel. Also, <imath> d = st </imath>, and by that time, Miguel traveled <imath> m </imath>, so <imath> m = v\left(\frac{2x - m}{5v}\right) </imath>, or <imath> 5m = 2x - m </imath>, <imath> 6m = 2x </imath>, <imath> 3m = x </imath>. The total distance from the park to the tree is <imath> 3m </imath>, and Miguel traversed <imath> m </imath>, giving us a total of <imath> \frac{m}{3m} = \boxed{\frac{1}{3}} </imath> the distance traveled.

~Pinotation

==Solution 3 (Set the Distance and Speed!)==

The distance doesn't seem to matter as if it did, then the problem would have told the distance, so lets say the distance is 30 units. Also the speed of Luna doesn't matter as the ratio of Luna's speed to Miguel's speed is 5:1, always the same. We can say that Luna goes 5 units a second, then that means that Miguel goes <imath>\frac{5}{5} =1</imath> units a second. Luna will reach the tree after <imath>\frac{30}{5} =6</imath> seconds. When Luna reaches the tree Miguel will be <imath>6 \times 1 = 6</imath> units from the entrance of the park. We can set up the equations: <imath>x+6</imath> and <imath>-5x+30</imath>, where x represents seconds as Miguel is 6 units from the entrance is walking away at a rate of 1 unit a second and Luna is 30 units from the entrance and is walking towards the entrance at a rate of 5 units a second. We can now set both equations equal together to find out how far away from the entrance they meet. <imath>x+6=-5x+30 \implies 6x=24 \implies x=4</imath>. This means that they meet 4 seconds after Luna reaches the tree, this means they meet after <imath>4+6=10</imath> seconds as Luna takes 6 seconds to reach the tree. In <imath>10</imath> seconds Miguel travels <imath>10 \times 1=10</imath> units, and <imath>\frac{10}{30} = \frac{1}{3}</imath>, giving us <imath>\boxed{\frac{1}{3}}</imath>
~ Shaarav14 for Carnage MS

==Solution 4==

Since Luna is 5 times faster than Miguel, Miguel gets <imath>\frac{1}{5}</imath>  of the way to the tree by the time Luna reaches the ball. The ratio of Miguel´s speed to Luna´s is 1:5, and the distance between Miguel and the tree is <imath>\frac{4}{5}</imath> the distance between the entrance and the tree. So Miguel walks another <imath>\frac{4}{5} \times \frac{1}{6}</imath> of the way from the entrance to the tree by the time Luna comes back to him. Therefore, Miguel walks <imath>\frac{1}{5} + \frac{4}{30}</imath> =<imath>\boxed{\frac{1}{3}}</imath> of the way to the tree from the entrance.
-Pillowwillowtree01

==Solution 5 (Quick)==

Since Luna runs 5 times faster than Miguel walks, by the time Luna reaches the tree, Miguel has walked <imath>\frac{1}{5}</imath> of the distance from the entrance to the tree. This eliminates answer choices <imath>\text{(A)}</imath> and <imath>\text{(B)}</imath>.

This is a multiple-choice problem with the remaining answers listed in increasing order, so we test the middle option, <imath>\text{(D)}</imath>, which corresponds to Miguel walking <imath>\frac{1}{3}</imath> of the distance.

If Miguel walks a total distance of <imath>\frac{1}{3}</imath>, then the additional distance he walks while Luna is running back toward him is <imath>\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{5}=\frac{2}{15}</imath>. Since Luna runs 5 times faster than Miguel walks, she covers <imath>5\cdot\frac{2}{15}=\frac{2}{3}</imath> of the distance on her return.

Thus, Luna runs the entire distance to the tree and <imath>\frac{2}{3}</imath> of the distance back, while Miguel walks <imath>\frac{1}{3}</imath> of the distance forward, so they meet at the same point. Therefore, the fraction of the distance Miguel covers is <imath>\boxed{\frac{1}{3}}</imath>.

~jeremyq

==Solution 6==
Because Luna is running five times as fast as Miguel, when the two meet, Luna will have run five times as far. We can call the distance from the place where Miguel threw the ball to the tree <imath>X</imath>, and the distance that Miguel runs <imath>Y</imath>. When the two meet they will have run a combined total of <imath>2X</imath>. Miguel runs <imath>Y</imath>, and because she runs five times as fast, Luna runs <imath>5Y</imath>. There combined total is therefore <imath>Y+5Y=6Y</imath>. So <imath>6Y=2x</imath>. The value we are trying to find is <imath>\frac{Y}{X}</imath>

We divide both sides of our equation by <imath>6x</imath> to get <imath>\frac{6Y}{6X}=\frac{2X}{6X}</imath>. This can be simplified to get <imath>\frac{Y}{X}=\frac{1}{3}</imath>. So the fraction of the distance to the tree that Miguel runs is <imath>\frac{Y}{X}=\boxed{\frac{1}{3}}</imath>


~Tgreyelephant

==Solution 7 - Cheese 🧀==
If you do not know how to use normal math to solve this question, you can also use a ruler and utilize the provided diagram.
